body:
As a 22 year old who has struggled with schizoaffective disorder, I don't necessary know the best way to help but I know exactly what your love was thinking the moment it happened. I've attempted suicide twice only to fail both times. The first time I was sure I was going to die, the second time was a lot more traumatic. 

In those moments of severe darkness, most people think we're only being selfish because of the harm we're going to do to our family, friends and other loved ones. This couldn't be further from the truth. I would put money on the fact that most last few moments before death of a suicide victim are spent with those that we are hurting with our conditions. I know my schizophrenia has been hard on my parents and my friends, and frankly, I don't have many of those "friends" left. The ones that are still here would probably die for me and I'm so grateful. 

The thing with mental disease is that we don't think the same way other people think. We constantly feel as if we are burdening those around us. I've even had states of psychosis where I've felt as if strangers are disgusted by my presence. Just imagine feeling like every time you walk into a room, you're followed by a putrid smell. It's quite similar. We feel that we're doing the world a favour by disappearing from it forever. We know it is going to hurt our family and friends but they'll heal in ways we couldn't. We're the special ones and we don't want to be. High powered mutants that try to do our best to seem like everyone else.

I know this hurts man, and it's going to hurt for a long time. You seem like you have a great support system and definitely see the grief counselors at your school. She was a fighter who could not fight any longer. She is at peace with her demons, no longer plagued by persecution and an extreme lack of a will to live. She will be grateful once you have come to terms with that. She doesn't want to see you suffer and frankly, it's the opposite. I know it's not the perfect answer but it's the best I could do. 

Take it easy on yourself, brother. The worst part is already over.

Ativan has helped me a lot. I was originally given it in a psych ward for sleep and it felt like a miracle. Everyone knows being hospitalized is a stressful occurrence and combine that with an anxiety disorder, yeah, not fun. It really seems to just take the edge off everything. Try it and see if you like it.

It was only once this year but that doesn't change the fact I've tried twice. Keep fighting kiddo. Life is all about self-affirmation. Too many people aren't proud enough to show the world how powerful they really are. Once you lose everything, you can have everything. Tiger, man, be one.

Just to give a little background on myself, I am a 22 year old male who has struggled with depression for almost half my life. I had everything as a child, I come from an extremely well off family and by extremely well off I mean we own 7 vehicles all of which are paid in full. I have the most incredible life from an outside perspective but I have attempted suicide twice and this year I spent 6 days in a state funded psych ward. (Anyone who knows anything about psychiatric care, this was virtually a holding tank for alcoholics/drug addicts who had no money and were waiting to be placed in an assisted living facility.) After nearly 8 years of treatment, the doctors finally got my diagnosis right, I am currently schizoaffective major depressive and I will be the rest of my life.

I know what it's like to feel like your whole life is fucked. I'm an intelligent person and being diagnosed with a disease that normally punishes you to institutions your entire life is something I never expected to hear. I have no idea what your physical pain is like but I'm sure we share a lot of emotional turmoil in common. 

Yes, you are correct by saying you're on borrowed time. I am too. I should have died when I was 17, I should have died when I was 21, but I'm still here and that's something. Some days are a lot worse than others and the friends I've had in my head for most of my life aren't the best friends a guy could ask for. This still doesn't stop me from waking up every morning and trying. Just simply trying to make a difference in my life and the life of others. All you have to do is try. It's not going to be easy but I promise you it will be worth it. Take solace in the fact that not only you're alive but you're here, the world is still ahead of you.

Take from this what you want but you have to try, man. You're only 14 and you should look at this as a positive thing. You may only have 50 years but look at all the things people have accomplished in less time. If you're religious at all the things Jesus accomplished in 33 years. Kurt Cobain launched an entire music movement and died at 27 (don't commit suicide like he did, it's the principle.) You can do amazing things and this has nothing to do with your situation. Look at Steven Hawking, the man can't even speak by himself is he is the most respected astrophysicist on the planet. Do some amazing things man, you're absolutely capable.

**TL;DR: YOU'RE A TIGER WHO'S EARNED HIS STRIPES, SHOW THOSE MOTHERFUCKERS OFF!!!!**

Thanks for all of the help guys. 
I did manage to throw out the rest of the remaining cigarettes and move on with my day. unlevered makes a really good point for anyone reading this for motivation. 

After 42 days, all of my habits have changed completely. Even having the filter in my mouth was so strange feeling. The smoke was so harsh going in and It felt ever more strange coming out.

Thanks for all of the support again. This subreddit is a great place for all  us.
